validation.rule: A typed claim (subject_kind, predicate, object_kind) is accepted iff the predicate is declared, both endpoint kinds are declared, and the exact (subject_kind, object_kind) pair is one of the predicate's allowed_pairs.
validation.scope_note: Text/span/citation grounding against the frozen snapshot is a later validation layer (Task 4); this schema validates types and pairs only.

decisions: Application added as a new entity kind: the frozen seed typed the whole system only via Command/Tool, which is why the budget-250 run typed daftprompt a Tool and rejected 'daftprompt uses akar'. Line 7 states daftprompt is a Rust app that uses akar, gitoxide, and the hybrid search indexer; line 141 confirms application-level ownership.
uses(Application, Tool) added: line 7 states the motivating fact and the frozen test input T0 records (subject Application, object Tool) as must-accept.

Subsystem added and uses(Application, Subsystem) allowed: the frozen R3 must-accept types the hybrid search indexer a Subsystem, not a Tool; forcing it into Tool would conflate the indexer subsystem with the search behavior it enables (recorded R3 rejection).

Documented relations R4, R5, R6, R7, R9 received their own predicates (serves_as, indexes, excludes, fuses, degrades_to) with their own kinds instead of being forced into the narrow seed shapes searches/uses; each predicate pair records its supporting snapshot line.

R8's object kind hint 'credential' maps to the seed kind Configuration, whose description explicitly names XIAOMI_API_KEY; no separate Credential kind was added and requires(Command, Configuration) already covers the R8 shape.

The seed's example_relations are copied into this artifact as schema sanity checks only (example_triples_role); they are never passed to the model as inference-time examples. No evidence exists that the local API supports relation examples at inference time.
Reference-set kind_hints are informal lowercase hints; the schema kinds above are the authoritative typing vocabulary (mapping recorded in reference_kind_hints).

No JointIE graph constraints (unique_head, acyclic, ...) are declared: they apply per relation label, not per canonical predicate, so variant labels would fragment them. All pair-level rules are enforced by validate_claim.

Task 4 (Epic 015): per-relation decision threshold 0.25 is declared for exactly the five predicates no Epic 014 checkpoint ever emitted (serves_as, indexes, excludes, fuses, degrades_to) and forwarded verbatim to JointSchema.relation(threshold=...); every other predicate keeps gliner2's default 0.5 decision bar so the one recovered relation (uses, R1) stays comparable to the canonical run. 0.25 is the JointIE tutorial's own demonstrated per-relation threshold (tutorial/15-joint_ie.md). Rejected alternative: 0.1 — more recall headroom but re-opens the misleading-claim flood `base` showed under loose gating (101/127 misleading); rejected alternative: 0.4 — too timid to move predicates that currently emit nothing.

Task 4 (Epic 015): the same five predicates' descriptions are rewritten to echo the frozen snapshot's own phrasing — the vocabulary is pulled from each predicate's added_task2 support lines (Epic 014 Task 2 audit trail) — per the GLiNER2 tutorial's clear, specific, example-grounded relation-description guidance. The pre-rewrite text is kept as description_previous and the grounding lines as description_support (description_origin: revised_task4).

Task 4 (Epic 015): per-predicate thresholds live on predicates[].threshold and are propagated to every derived JointIE label by derive_joint_ie_labels at load time; the model_mapping.joint_ie.labels embed keeps its label-shape-only key set (canonical_predicate, head, tail, description) so Epic 014's loader-derivation equality holds unchanged. Thresholds are not JointIEConfig fields — the run manifest identifies them via the schema artifact sha256.
model_schema_limitations: gliner2 2.0.0 JointIE typed endpoints are a Cartesian product: joint_ie/constraints.py TypedEndpoints.allows accepts an edge iff the head type is in head_types AND the tail type is in tail_types, and joint_ie/candidates.py CandidateBuilder pairs role spans with itertools.product over head x tail types. A single relation cannot declare 'these pairs only'.

Chosen mapping: when a predicate's allowed pairs equal the product of distinct head x distinct tail kinds, one JointIE relation is emitted with multi-type head/tail. Otherwise pairs are grouped by subject kind (each group is a lossless product of one head type with its tail types); the largest group (ties: alphabetical head kind) keeps the bare predicate name and the rest become predicate__2, predicate__3, ... (e.g. uses -> uses [Application -> Subsystem|Tool], uses__2 [Command -> Tool]).

Validation always enforces the canonical declared pairs, never the label-level product: uses(Command, Subsystem) is rejected even though the model labels uses and uses__2 jointly mention Command and Subsystem.
Independent extract_relations (tutorial 6) carries no endpoint typing at all; canonical predicate names map 1:1 to relation labels and the typed pairs are enforced post-hoc by the validator.
JointIE long-text extraction keeps a relation only when both endpoint mentions fall in the same chunk; chunk boundaries/overlaps are recorded by the Task 3 adapter, not by this schema.
